annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 126 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Gods phase.

annotations.annotation_text: Egyptian eschatology "set" on page 126 ("The Quiz Chapter"): within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones, HCE appears as the dismembered Osiris and ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs. Mark Troy's research traces how Joyce embedded the Papyrus of Ani's resurrection liturgy throughout this Age of Gods passage — the dream-journey through the underworld (Tuat) toward solar rebirth.

annotations.annotation_text: Shem the Penman acts as the interrogator, asking twelve riddles, while his brother Shaun provides the answers.
sources: Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Shaun provides the twelve answers to Shem's riddles, but often in a reversed, convoluted, or entirely evasive manner.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8

annotations.annotation_text: The Mookse and the Gripes fable: The Mookse represents Shaun and the Pope/Catholicism, while the Gripes represents Shem and Protestantism/heresy.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Professor Jones: A caricature of the officious academic, delivering a pedantic lecture that introduces the fable of the Mookse and the Gripes.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.annotation_text: The answers to the quiz questions frequently manifest as doubles or alter-egos of HCE, expanding his identity across space and time.
sources: Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
